label: rem:categorical-coordinate-ring-dedup
title: $R[i,q^{\pm1}]$ as the ambient deformation ring: deduplicating four complexifications
html:
Downstream applications of R[i, q^{\pm 1}]. Recognizing the categorical-coordinate ring as the ambient deformation ring (4.25.8) deduplicates four ad-hoc complexification patterns:

  1. Here. The substitution q = e^{i\varTheta} used in the commutative-limit remark is not an external complexification. The element e^{i\varTheta} = \cos\varTheta + i\sin\varTheta is a unit in R[i] via the Euler identity. Compute q - q^{-1} = 2i\sin\varTheta entirely inside R[i, q^{\pm 1}] without enlarging the categorical ground ring.
  2. Witness computations. The complex arithmetic in isospin-mass-tower-collapse and the broader mass-tower pipeline is justified categorically as a single specialisation R[i, q^{\pm 1}] \to \mathbb{C} via q \mapsto q_0. Apply the universal property of the categorical-coordinate ring once, rather than complexifying ad hoc per script.
  3. Wick-rotation and complex-substrate remarks. The blocks 4.22.5 and 4.17.14 previously complexified in isolation (introducing i for the half-plane swap, the CR structure, and the substrate value). Both invocations of i are realisations of the single categorical coordinate of 4.25.8, under the \mathrm{Gal}(R[i]/R) = \mathbb{Z}_2 orientation choice of 4.25.4.
  4. Curves over the substrate. It is customary to introduce the hyperelliptic quintic \mathcal{X}_5: y^2 = x^5 - 1 (8.3.1) and the Descartes elliptic curve \mathcal{E}_q (8.8.15) "over \mathbb{C}" with \zeta_5 = e^{2\pi i/5} as a complex root of unity. In the categorical-coordinate framework, these curves live over R[i, q^{\pm 1}] at q = q_0. The fifth roots of unity \zeta_5^k are the five geometric points of \mathrm{Spec}(R[i, q^{\pm 1}]) where the chart-transition coefficient hits \zeta_5^k.

In each case, the unification supplies a single categorical coordinate ring: the algorithmic computations and proofs remain identical, while their ambient base ring is consolidated into R[i, q^{\pm 1}].
